thread:
incident-bot: Pager: SEV-1 serving-runtime: multi-GPU collectives failing on tp-job-441 (nccL timeouts + CUDA OOM). Impact: several requests failing with 500s, automated fallback attempted but some workers restarted. Paging #incidents.

oncall-alex: ack I'm on it, grabbing context. Which fleets/regions affected?

maria: seeing errors across 3 nodes in us-west1-g, nodes gpu-pool-03-{12,13,14} all reporting NCCL TIMEOUT in logs. Customer-facing error rate up ~12% on hosted API.

sven: logs: ```
E NCCL WARN call to allreduce timed out after 120s
E CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY: failed to allocate 512MB for kernel workspace
E worker[13]: container exited with code 137 (OOM)
```

irene: any recent deploys to the model or runtime? deploy-bot: release 2026.03.15-77 rolled at 16:12 UTC to the hosted cluster, no rollback triggered.

oncall-alex: okay, looks like a correlated regression but could be capacity pressure + longer seq lengths. What's the model and batch profiles?

maria: model: redwood/rw-13b-compat@v2 (quantized), avg seq length 1024 for affected requests, burst of 2k qps during spike. Batching config set to 64 tokens per batch.

samir: noticed KV cache growth on pipeline-parallel shards, memory not reclaimed between sessions. Could be a leak in runtime 77.

oncall-alex: immediate mitigation plan: 1) evade multi-GPU collectives by routing to single-GPU fallbacks for latency-sensitive customers; 2) scale up dedicated capacity as temporary cushion; 3) cordon the three nodes and drain to avoid flapping restarts.

maria: starting traffic routing change now for the hosted route 'gen-prod-v2' -> switching policy to prefer single-gpu compatible variants. Will monitor errors.

sven: running drain on nodes: ```kubectl cordon gpu-pool-03-12 && kubectl drain gpu-pool-03-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force```

irene: also increasing model replica count in single-gpu pool by +4: ```rmctl scale --cluster hosted-usw1 --pool single-gpu --model redwood/rw-13b-compat@v2 --replicas +4```

deploy-bot: Note: rollback possible with `release rollback 2026.03.15-77` — will require traffic cutover window ~3m.

oncall-alex: let's hold rollback for now unless errors persist after routing/scale. Rolling back would be heavier.

maria: traffic routing change deployed. Error rate for gen-prod-v2 dropped from 12% -> 3% in 4m. Latency stable for most customers.

sven: node cordon + drain in progress for the 3 nodes. One node already restarted twice — suspect underlying GPU driver OOM chain.

samir: capturing full heap / nvprof traces from the restarted node before it's reprovisioned. Command: ```gcloud compute instances get-serial-port-output gpu-pool-03-13 --port 1```

irene: any customer escalations? CX reports a few 500s from a mid-market customer, but they are on a dedicated tenant — looks like they hit the hosted path fallback for some requests. CCing @maria to follow up.

maria: reaching out to CS with a summary and temporary mitigation steps (routing to single-GPU, ETA for full remediation TBD).

oncall-alex: plan for deeper analysis after stabilization: - collect nvml, dmesg, and runtime heap dumps - check for regression in memory reclamation code introduced in 2026.03.15-77 - run stress job with long seqs on a staging shard to reproduce leak

sven: collecting artifacts now: ```tar -czf /tmp/artifacts-gpu-03-13.tgz /var/log/nvidia* /var/log/containers/* /srv/runtime/dumps``` then uploading to s3.

samir: started stress replay on staging with similar traffic profile; injecting long sessions. If leak reproduces we can iterate on a patch.

maria: monitoring metrics: token cost per request spiked correlating with OOM events. Will set an alert rule to detect growing KV cache size per run.

oncall-alex: good. Oncall to keep this channel updated every 10m until we close. Next steps if errors don't fall: 1) rollback release 77; 2) enable stricter per-session memory caps in runtime; 3) full customer incident follow-up.

irene: question - do we have an automated fallback for TP->DP conversion on the runtime? if not, might be useful for future.

sven: we have a soft-fallback that tries to use compatible single-gpu variants when communicator init fails, but it doesn't always trigger if container dies quickly. Need more robust failover.

maria: error rate now at 1.1% — still above baseline but much better. Drains complete on 2/3 nodes, third node is unresponsive so infra started reprovision.

samir: pulled heapshot from the bad worker: looks like persistent tensor handles in KV cache not freed between sequences. Attaching snippet: ```
runtime: kv_cache size=14.7GB after request complete
runtime: expected < 1GB
```

oncall-alex: this points to regression in cache eviction logic. Please open a P0 ticket and assign to eng-runtime for a patch. Keep current mitigations in place until fix validated.

maria: opened ticket ENG-RT-2026 with logs and artifacts. Tagging @sven @samir.

deploy-bot: Hotfix workflow: create branch `hotfix/rt-cache-evict-20260315`, run ci, canary to 2 nodes.

sven: starting a hotfix PR now to re-enable aggressive eviction strategy. Will run unit + e2e tests, then canary.

oncall-alex: thanks everyone. I'll prepare a short incident summary for ops and CS once we have hotfix canary results. For now, customer impact reduced, no active outages after routing + scale.

maria: closing paging loop for now — will reopen if regression appears. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident status update: SEV-1 -> SEV-2 (partial mitigation applied). Next update in 30m or on status change.
